memory_update.text: LOPE should remain a priority direct-exposure candidate for the online higher-ed student acquisition/services node because its disclosed service agreements map closely to marketing, communication, technology, academic, counseling, and back-office infrastructure.
STRA is a direct operator plus employer/workforce education platform; future layers should separate owned-university exposure from Education Technology Services exposure.
COUR is a small-cap platform candidate with direct university/degree and enterprise workforce-learning exposure, but evidence must confirm degree-program economics and institutional durability.

LRN is an adjacent online education infrastructure candidate; include in later layers only if Career Learning and adult/workforce training exposure are material enough versus K-12 virtual-school exposure.

Need a separate supplier/software pass for student-information systems, CRM/admissions software, retention analytics, testing/proctoring, and enrollment-marketing vendors; many relevant assets may be private or embedded inside broader enterprise software companies.

LOPE should remain a priority underfollowed candidate for the online higher-ed fixed-cost stack because it maps directly to outsourced university services, partner programs, online enrollment support, and healthcare/hybrid education infrastructure.

STRA is a second-order candidate through Workforce Edge, Sophia Learning, and employer-affiliated enrollment; later layers should separate its owned-university economics from supplier-like education technology services.

COUR is a platform-layer candidate for university degree distribution and workforce credentials; evidence quality is good, but purity depends on degree/enterprise mix and post-Udemy integration economics.
KLTR is a speculative_shadow infrastructure supplier below the preferred market-cap range; keep only if education customer concentration, retention, and cash runway support chokepoint relevance.

Major student information systems, LMS, and OPM assets such as Ellucian, Blackboard/Anthology, Instructure, and 2U/edX may be private, delisted, or no longer clean US-listed exposures; later passes should map private chokepoints as customer/supplier anchors even if not investable directly.

LOPE is the strongest direct underfollowed public-market candidate for the online higher-ed fixed-cost stack because its disclosed service bundle maps to marketing, lead acquisition, admissions, financial aid, advising, LMS, CRM, student records, course development, faculty support, scheduling, and hybrid healthcare lab infrastructure.

STRA should be tracked not only as an online higher-ed operator but as an employer-channel and education-benefits infrastructure asset through ETS, Sophia Learning, Workforce Edge, and employer-affiliated enrollment.

COUR remains relevant to the node as a small-cap platform layer for degrees, campus, enterprise, government, credit-bearing certificates, and workforce credentials, but evidence must verify institutional durability and degree economics.

Need a later pass on private or recently delisted OPM/student-information-system vendors such as 2U, Instructure, PowerSchool, Anthology, Ellucian, and niche enrollment-marketing firms because many direct chokepoint assets may not currently be US-listed.

The core bottleneck is not content alone; it is the capitalized and operationally complex stack of student acquisition, compliance-aware admissions, financial aid, advising, retention analytics, SIS/LMS/CRM integration, course development, and employer/workforce distribution.
LOPE is the clean public reference anchor for outsourced online higher-education enrollment, marketing, student services, SIS/LMS support, curriculum, and compliance infrastructure.
STRA should remain in the underfollowed lane because its ETS, Sophia, Workforce Edge, and employer-affiliated enrollment data may indicate a less obvious student-acquisition and retention channel.
COUR is a platform/distribution candidate rather than a full OPM; promote only if degree, enterprise, campus, or government credential evidence shows durable institutional adoption.

CVSA is a demand-side and operator-scale hypothesis, not a pure infrastructure supplier; useful for monitoring healthcare-workforce education as a high-need vertical within online/hybrid higher education.

Need a later pass for private OPM comparables and public software suppliers to universities, including CRM, SIS, retention analytics, identity verification, proctoring, and admissions-marketing vendors.

node: Online higher-education enrollment, marketing, student services, and retention infrastructure
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: This Layer 1B pass maps direct US-listed exposure to the fixed-cost stack needed to scale online higher education: enrollment marketing, advising, student support, degree/program platform distribution, employer/workforce channels, and retention infrastructure. The strongest direct public-market exposures found are not mega-cap software names, but education-services operators whose business models depend on student acquisition, online delivery, employer partnerships, and support services. Grand Canyon Education and Strategic Education are the cleanest higher-education/service-stack names; Coursera is a smaller-cap platform exposure; Stride is adjacent through career learning and online education infrastructure but less pure to higher-ed degree programs. Layer 1B expands the universe around the fixed-cost stack needed to scale online higher education: enrollment marketing, admissions/advising, university partner services, course-development support, learning platforms, rich-media delivery, employer-to-university pathways, and retention infrastructure. The strongest underfollowed candidates are not all labeled as 'education' stocks: some appear as business services, enterprise software, or workforce platforms. This pass found one relatively pure service-provider name, two platform/workforce intermediaries, and one micro-cap infrastructure exception. No buy/sell recommendation is made. Expanded the underfollowed universe around the fixed-cost online higher-education stack: student acquisition, admissions, advising, employer channels, degree platforms, retention infrastructure,
